question: A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days. After 12 days, A leaves and B completes the remaining work in 10 days. A alone can complete the work in how many days?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining work of (A + B) for 8 days (20 − 12) is finished by B in 10 days.

8 × (A + B) = 10 × B ⇒ 8A + 8B = 10B ⇒ 8A = 2B ⇒ B = 4A.

Efficiency ratio A : B = 1 : 4. Total efficiency = 1 + 4 = 5.

Total work = Total efficiency × Total time = 5 × 20 = 100 units.

Time taken by A alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of A = 100 ÷ 1 = 100 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 20 days.

Work done by (A + B) before A leaves = 12 days.

Time taken by B to finish remaining work = 10 days.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total work = 20 units (LCM of 20).

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 20 ÷ 20 = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Work done by (A + B) in 12 days = 1 × 12 = 12 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 20 − 12 = 8 units.

⇒ B completes 8 units in 10 days.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 8 ÷ 10 = 0.8 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of A = 20 ÷ 0.2 = 100 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If A is twice as efficient as B, A will take half the time B takes.

Combined Work Formula

If A takes x days and B takes y days, together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time and Work, where an inlet pipe has positive efficiency and an outlet pipe (leak) has negative efficiency.</p
